claims.statement: The local StoreKit configuration defines family-shareable products `com.akinokaede.termind.pro.annual` at 3.99 per year and `com.akinokaede.termind.pro` at 9.99 as a non-consumable, with the annual product in the `Termind Pro` group and a two-week free introductory offer.
The local StoreKit fixture contains English, Simplified Chinese, and Traditional Chinese names and descriptions for both the annual and lifetime products.

RevenueCat resolves only the configured entitlement after rejecting failed verification: an active expiration-free entitlement grants lifetime access, active trials/subscriptions require future expiry, billing-issue grace requires a future grace deadline, and refunds, expired and billing-retry phases do not grant Pro; a cached active flag cannot extend an expired subscription.

RevenueCatProPurchaseService fetches current CustomerInfo for refresh, falls back to cached info if fetching fails and listens to customerInfoStream; the controller coalesces simultaneous refreshes and supersedes an older in-flight result with a newer stream update, keeping established status on a later failed refresh but marking a failed initial refresh verificationFailed.

ProAccessController gates assistant use, terminal file upload, remote MCP, built-in MCP server, Vault sync and unlimited Metrics through current entitlement status; a denied require presents the paywall, and this Pro feature vocabulary does not make the Mac-only built-in MCP server available on iOS.

Mac and mobile wrappers both present RevenueCatUI PaywallView with controller-derived ProPaywallState custom variables, show loading and unconfigured-service fallbacks, block initiating purchases while access exists, refresh after completed purchase or restore and suppress the first post-purchase SDK dismissal to leave the account variant visible; remote dashboard content rather than local shared paywall code owns offer layout.

RevenueCatCommerceTests exercise configured entitlement, deadline and refund resolution plus controller refresh, stream and error behavior with fake or decoded CustomerInfo; ProPaywallStateTests check remote paywall variable mapping, while the opt-in StoreKitTrialTests checks only local fixture metadata, not a live purchase or remotely rendered paywall. The former ProOffer/ProPaywall presentation and rendering suites are absent.

Localized final App Store JPG boards are organized into English, Simplified Chinese, and Traditional Chinese sets for Mac, iPhone 6.5-inch, and iPad 13-inch; these exports are distinct from the screenshot captures and device-frame inputs used for the website.

StoreKitTrialTests is a manually enabled serialized SKTestSession suite loading StoreKit/Termind.storekit to verify annual and lifetime product types and Family Sharing plus the annual yearly period and two-week zero-price introductory trial; it does not purchase, restore or verify RevenueCat entitlement, offerings, eligibility or remote paywall behavior.

Applying a granting subscription status with future expiration cancels the old deadline task and schedules a RevenueCat refresh at that deadline rather than directly revoking access; applying another status replaces the task, teardown cancels it, and Mac activation or iOS scene activation also refreshes access.

Separate Mac and mobile signing entitlement files both declare the CloudKit container, webcredentials domain and bundle-derived keychain group, while Mac additionally grants App Sandbox device/network/file permissions; these signed capabilities are separate from StoreKit fixture products and RevenueCat entitlement resolution.

The built-in MCP server's Pro gate is wired in the Mac model and settings through `.mcpServer`, whereas mobile remote MCP actions use `.remoteMCP`; the shared Pro feature enumeration is not evidence that the built-in server is available on mobile.

Live Pro access requires valid bundled RevenueCat key and entitlement configuration; a missing or invalid config leaves the controller verificationFailed without an alternate StoreKit observer, and release builds reject test_ keys while DEBUG allows them.

Both app Info.plist files substitute the RevenueCat API key and entitlement ID from Xcode build settings; the project specifies termind_pro as the entitlement ID, so the signed app's resolved values and matching dashboard entitlement/product mapping must be checked independently from the StoreKit fixture.

RevenueCat purchase service configures StoreKit 2, informational verification, preferred UI language from stored AppLanguage and no automatic device identifier collection; it uses anonymous RevenueCat IDs and avoids a device or iCloud account based custom ID.

On a non-test store, the service attempts syncPurchases once per anonymous app user when a valid fetched status does not grant access, persisting a successful migration marker; this import of pre-integration Apple purchases is distinct from a user's remote restore action.

ProPaywallState maps subscription phases, renewal and ownership to nonlocalized RevenueCat dashboard protocol values and separately supplies access, management permission, Family Sharing and optional expiration; manage is true only for purchaser-owned subscriptions, not family-shared or lifetime purchases.

Both native RevenueCatUI wrappers reset processing on purchase/restore cancellation or failure and on disappear, and keep the remote account variant visible after purchase; Mac presents a single owning window sheet while iOS presents from MobileRootView.

The local fixture's product descriptions, two-week offer and price do not supply native paywall feature rows or guarantee RevenueCat eligibility or dashboard trial disclosure; current native views render the SDK paywall using remote configuration and controller-derived variables.
